speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) with the replacement of Network Capacity Factor to exclude ridership in the new Fare Adjustment Formula, how will fare changes take into account lower ridership or demand; and (b) besides the Thomson-East Coast Line, whether the Capacity Adjustment Factor has considered the anticipated opening of additional stations in the Downtown Line, Circle Line and Jurong Region Line from 2025 to 2028.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: There will be no changes in fares until then.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The new fare formula replaces the Network Capacity Factor with the Capacity Adjustment Factor, or NCF with "C".

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Both measure public transport capacity, which benefits commuters through improved connectivity and faster journey times.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The difference is that NCF was computed every year and factors in ridership alongside capacity – it is positive when capacity grows faster than ridership and negative when ridership grows faster than capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In its first three years, the NCF ranged from 1.6% to 3.9%.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But the NCF was not designed for situations such as the COVID-19 pandemic, when ridership fell sharply.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As a result, NCF was suspended when it spiked to 50% in the 2021 Fare Review Exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This reflects both the actual and planned growth in public transport capacity from 2020 to 2026, largely arising from the opening of the Thomson-East Coast Line (TEL).

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Aside from TEL, "C" also takes into account short segments of the North-East, Downtown and Circle Lines which will open during this period.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Jurong Region Line is slated to open from 2027 and will only be considered in the next fare formula review.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The PTC opted to exclude ridership from "C" because of uncertainties in ridership recovery over the next few years, with changing commuting patterns and flexible work arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: While ridership at the system level is at about 90% of pre-COVID-19 levels, the recovery has been uneven.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: For example, journeys to the Downtown Core are still at about 70% of pre-COVID-19 levels and ridership could be considered in subsequent fare formula reviews when ridership fully recovers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In the meantime, fixing "C" at 1.1% for the next five years will reduce potential variability in fares arising from the uncertain recovery of ridership.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As a result, households now spend a smaller share of their income on public transport compared to a decade ago.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In addition to the broad-based subsidy that all commuters enjoy, more than two million commuters – one in two Singaporeans – including students, seniors, persons with disabilities (PwDs) and lower-wage workers pay concessionary fares which are up to 70% lower than adult fares.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And these groups either receive their concession cards automatically or are invited to apply for them.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Monthly passes can help heavy users cap their public transport expenditure.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: For example, seniors can purchase a monthly concession pass for $64 to enjoy unlimited journeys on buses and trains for about $2 per day.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Concession card holders can purchase a monthly pass at mass rapid transit stations and bus interchanges or through the SimplyGo mobile app or website if they have upgraded their cards.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Singaporean and Permanent Resident adults can similarly enjoy unlimited journeys by applying for an identifiable card and purchasing a monthly pass through the same means.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The PTC had suggested that more could be done to raise awareness of these passes and prompt heavy public transport users who benefit from such passes to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Government will look into how to support this suggestion.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Arising from the fare adjustment last year, 600,000 PTVs with a value of $30 are available for resident households with monthly household income per person of not more than $1,600.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The 240,000 households that received a PTV from the previous exercise, and continue to meet the eligibility criteria, have automatically received their PTVs via post.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Other eligible households can apply online or at the community centres.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Those not eligible can also appeal online or at community centres.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This information is publicised via posters in buses and public transport nodes.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And I seek Members' assistance to inform your residents as well, so that more can benefit from these schemes.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I also wish to thank the members of the PTC led by Mdm Chairperson, our Nominated Member of Parliament, hon Ms Janet Ang.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My supplementary question is: given the connectivity plans for the future lines and the projected increase in ridership, does the Ministry foresee that the current transport subsidy assistance schemes available will be tweaked further?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For instance, increasing the PTVs or maybe have a more calibrated approach to the PTVs, as I had suggested in one of my Parliamentary Questions – for instance, for those who do not qualify strictly for the PTVs, maybe a smaller quantum of less than $30 be provided to cushion the impact of any projected increment.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: His first point, his essential point is whether transport subsidies – and I think by this he means specifically for commuters – will be increased, given that we are increasing the scale.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, if I may, as a starting point, reiterate that in the provision of public transport in Singapore, our aspiration has always been to raise the quality and accessibility.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: At the same time, to make sure that it is affordable for Singaporeans and also ensure the long-term financial sustainability of the provision.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is essentially the triangulation that the PTC seeks to achieve through its recommendations and the Government seeks to attain through the implementation of various policy measures.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Having said that, in terms of the level of subsidy that we accord public transport, it is at different levels.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we do that for seniors, for PwDs, for lower-income workers, for students and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And then, finally, when there is a fare adjustment made – in other words a fare increase – in tandem with that, we typically implement PTVs or issue them especially to help those who are in the more vulnerable brackets, and that is what we did in the last exercise.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, whether it is in terms of the systemic support through subsidies, through the targeted support that we do through concession fares and so on, and also through specific moves in tandem with any fare adjustment through PTVs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And we are continuing to see how we can improve this to better meet the needs of specific groups of commuters.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And I thank the Minister for his reply.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have one supplementary question and one suggestion.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The supplementary question is in relation to whether the Ministry has been tracking the redemption rates of the concessions, our monthly passes and the PTVs respectively?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Are we beginning to see an uptick trend in terms of these applications and approvals, from pre-COVID-19 to post-COVID-19 period?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And the other point, in relation to the suggestion to increase awareness and provide more help, is whether we can explore to train the relevant staff at the respective train stations, where members of the public or commuters applying for the concession passes can also enquire about the availability and application of the PTVs?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Whether we track for concessions, basically, this is a function of how much the concession card holder uses, whether it is for a train or a bus, because every time they use it, they will tap and get that discounted fare – that is the concession card formulation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because when you look at the Downtown Core, the recovery is lower.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But when you look at some of the heartland areas and the industrial areas, it is much stronger.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think it is a reflection of changing habits and work-from-home, and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we need to see how this thing pans out.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But specifically, then, what it means is we think the usage patterns amongst some of the specific groups, like seniors and so on, has recovered in tandem with this overall rise.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I would be happy to give a more specific response if the Member wants to file something more precise on that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Then, on the issue of take-up rates of the PTVs, as I said, they work in different tranches.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: One tranche is when we just send it out by post to all those who were previously eligible and continue to be eligible; and they get it automatically.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Then, there is the second tranche where they can apply and the application can go through the website and also to the community centre and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And then, the third tranche is when they make appeals and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The key point is we are ready to help not just as a first cut, but also where there are instances where additional help is needed, we are happy to look into this and render the necessary support.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the point about staff being well trained, I agree with the Member fully.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is not just about how you can access concession fares or PTVs and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is also about things like inclusivity, rendering assistance to those who may have difficulties moving around, information on wayfinding and so on, because these things are important complements to what we already do through the infrastructure.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, the Member's point is well taken, and this is an ongoing effort to improve the frontline service level that we have in our public transport system.
